newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Egypt plans to accelerate sell-off of firms--RFTV.
newsitem.headline: Egypt plans to accelerate sell-off of firms--RFTV.

text.p: Egypt plans to sell off 30 state enterprises this year and another 80-100 public firms in 1998, Egyptian Public Sector Minister Atef Ebeid said on Thursday.
Ebeid, who traveled to the U.N. for the Earth Summit, told Reuters Financial Television that by the end of 1997 Egypt will have sold 108 firms out of the 314 enterprises in its privatization program.
The pace of the asset sales will increase next year, Ebeid said.
"We will be moving a little bit faster next year," Ebeid said. "We will be able to put to the market 80-100 companies."
He said the government planned to complete the privatization program by the turn of the millenium.
Ebeid said he was not concerned about market talk that the Cairo stock exchange, which has declined in recent months, needed fresh issues.
"There is a flood of capital moving to Egypt as an attractive emerging market," Ebeid said. "That needs an increase in the supply, and we intend to do so."
He also said Egypt expected to receive $2.0-$3.0 billion in fresh investment next year as a result of that Egypt's new investor incentive law passed last month.
